# `tui log` for [viewers](/commands/categories/viewers.md)

<div class='command-title'>Add an append-only log view. Streamed rows appear at the bottom.</div>

## Command Type

`built-in`

## Signature

```> tui log {flags} (source)```

## Flags

 -  `--title {string}`: Border title, in place of the widget's name. Counts, state, or the previewed file follow in parentheses.
 -  `--border {string}`: Border lines, named like `table --theme` (rounded, double, heavy, ...).
 -  `--max-lines {int}`: Keep only the last N lines (default 10000).
 -  `--id {string}`: Widget id.
 -  `--focus`: Start with this widget focused.
 -  `--data {any}`: Data for this widget alone, instead of the outer pipeline's. Not with --from or a closure.
 -  `--from {string}`: Id of the table, tree, or select whose highlighted row drives this widget.

## Parameters

 -  `source`: Closure over the highlighted row of --from, or of the nearest table, tree, or select, whose output is shown.


## Input/output types:

| input   | output |
| ------- | ------ |
| nothing | tui    |
| tui     | tui    |
| any     | tui    |
## Examples

Live log of a slow stream
```nu
> 1.. | each {|n| sleep 100ms; $"tick ($n)"} | tui label --titlebar "ticks" | tui log | tui run

```

## Notes
Follows the tail as new items arrive. Mouse wheel and Up/Down scroll; scrolling up pauses follow until you hit the bottom again. `--max-lines` keeps that many newest lines in the view. A stream keeps its newest 100,000 rows, or `--max-lines` if that is more.

With a closure the log shows the closure's output for the highlighted row of a table, tree, or select instead of the piped data, e.g. `tui log --from table-0 {|row| open $row.name | lines }`. It follows the one named by `--from`, else the focused one, else the nearest, which may be on another tab page. A closure with no table, tree, or select to follow is an error when the TUI starts; to show a stream, pipe it in without a closure.
